product.ta-dario286.summary: Documented 12 MHz 80286 desktop, equivalent to the Olivetti PCS 286
product.ta-dario286.history: Triumph-Adler, owned by Olivetti from 1986, marketed this platform as Dario 286 and P35 while the same motherboard was sold as the Olivetti PCS 286. It is not documented whether it was a Triumph-Adler design adopted by Olivetti, an Olivetti commission or one product sold under two brands. The exceptionally detailed June 1990 technical training manual identifies the actual board assemblies, chip set, clocks, memory population, jumpers, CMOS layout and service diagnostics.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cpu_bus: Intel 80286 at 12 MHz with one wait state; Extended Setup F7 switches memory and I/O operation between 12 and 6 MHz. An Intel 80287 is optional.
product.ta-dario286.technical.chipset: The service manual identifies the G2 GC101A and GC102 controller pair plus the proprietary IOC. BluMach uses the GC10x core with the proven PCS 286 IOC02 behavior.
product.ta-dario286.technical.memory: CSAA03/06/09 board variants and SIMM combinations provide 512 KB, 640 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB or 4 MB. The standard 1 MB arrangement is 512 KB soldered plus two 256 KB SIMMs.
product.ta-dario286.technical.storage: WD37C65B floppy control and IDE disks. Documented factory drives include Conner CP3022/CP3024 20 MB and CP346/CP3044 40 MB models.
product.ta-dario286.technical.jumpers: A11 enables or disables the password; B07/B08 select DD or HD floppy operation; X04 selects the SIMM or system-board memory bank.
product.ta-dario286.technical.cmos: The DS1287 exposes 128 CMOS bytes. The manual documents floppy at 10h, disk at 12h/19h/1Ah, equipment at 14h, memory at 15h–18h and 30h–31h, language at 1Bh, video at 1Ch, password at 37h–3Fh and checksums at 2Eh/2Fh and 7Eh/7Fh.
product.ta-dario286.technical.diagnostic: Resident Diagnostics run at boot. Customer Test is supplied on CSFA12 and started with CUSTOMER; its floppy test writes to disk number 1.
product.ta-dario286.technical.identity: The Dario and PCS 286 are the same TA-built platform. In the absence of a separately labelled Dario dump, BluMach deliberately uses the preserved PCS 286 BIOS 1.37/1.42 set rather than inventing firmware differences.
product.ta-dario286.technical.verified: Shares the booted PCS 286 implementation: BIOS 1.42, Setup, Resident Diagnostics, MS-DOS, GC101/102 memory-control test and 20/40 MB IDE configurations.
product.ta-dario286.technical.limitation: The original keyboard-controller firmware is not preserved and is represented by the Olivetti-compatible KBC behavior. A Dario-labelled BIOS dump would still be valuable for archival comparison. As on the PCS 286, the Setup RAM/IO frequency is applied approximately; the password keyboard-lock mode is not emulated and the keyboard repeat rate follows the host computer.

product.ta-dario286.creation.models: Two 1.44 MB floppy drives; one 1.44 MB floppy drive with a 20 MB hard disk; or one 1.44 MB floppy drive with a 40 MB hard disk
product.ta-dario286.creation.note: Same choices as the Olivetti PCS 286, which shares the board and BIOS: two 1.44 MB floppy drives, or one floppy drive with a 20 or 40 MB disk (the Dario manual documents Conner CP3022/CP3024 and CP346/CP3044). The disk takes the second bay, so disk profiles have one floppy drive. PCS 286 BIOS 1.42 is used because no Dario-labelled BIOS is preserved; none of these choices has been checked on the Dario yet.
product.ta-dario286.creation.sound.sbpro: Sound Blaster Pro (8-bit stereo PCM, later upgrade)
Sound Blaster Pro 2 (8-bit stereo PCM, later upgrade)
product.ta-dario286.creation.sound_286_n: Only sound options with a 286-compatible software path are offered. Creative's Pro manuals include 286 systems; Windows applications require the stated Windows version. SB16 and other cards without a verified 286 setup/driver package are omitted. Audio on this Dario 286 remains to be tested.
product.ta-dario286.creation.storage.one: Commercial: one 1.44 MB floppy drive + 20 MB IDE hard disk
Commercial: one 1.44 MB floppy drive + 40 MB IDE hard disk
product.ta-dario286.creation.upgrades_no: Internal Paradise PVGA1A uses the motherboard BIOS; no separate VGA ROM is needed. RAM options are 1, 2 and 4 MB. Sound cards are optional user upgrades, not documented Triumph-Adler sales configurations. ISA compatibility is inferred from the machine bus and emulator devices; audio and expanded-RAM diagnostics await validation on this profile.
